prompt:
The period T of oscillation of a liquid column of length L in an open U-tube manometer is modelled by the formula:
T = 2 * pi * sqrt(L / (2 * g))
where g is the acceleration of free fall.
(a) State the SI base units of the quantity L / g. [1]
(b) Show that the right-hand side of the equation simplifies to the SI base unit of second (s). [1]
(c) State and explain whether the formula is homogeneous with respect to SI base units. [1]

mark_scheme.criterion: State that 2*pi and 1/sqrt(2) are dimensionless, and sqrt(s^2) = s.
State that both sides have base unit s, therefore the equation is homogeneous.

hints: Evaluate L / g first, then take the square root.
Remember that 2 * pi is a pure dimensionless number.
solution: (a) [L / g] = m / (m s^-2) = s^2. (b) [sqrt(L / (2 * g))] = sqrt(s^2) = s; the constants 2*pi and sqrt(2) are dimensionless. (c) The left-hand side [T] = s matches the right-hand side, so the equation is homogeneous.
teacher_walkthrough: (a) Length L has unit m; g has unit m s^-2. Thus [L / g] = m / (m s^-2) = s^2.
(b) Taking the square root of s^2 gives s. The factors 2*pi and 1/sqrt(2) are dimensionless pure numbers.
(c) Period T is time (s). Since both sides have the base unit s, the equation is homogeneous.

provenance.independence_statement: Authored using U-tube liquid column oscillation to test square root unit simplification.
